jobs.description:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a member of the Supercomputer Physical Infrastructure team, you will design, build, and activate control systems for some of the world’s most technically advanced AI training campuses. As a Controls Engineer, you will develop and commission automated solutions that keep cooling plants, electrical distribution, liquid-cooling loops, and data halls running at the pace of compute demand. The automation and controls team designs, builds, and commissions complete control systems from the ground up. We are looking for talent with a proven track record in developing, troubleshooting, and maintaining control systems for production and critical infrastructure. This position is based in Memphis, TN, with work across the Memphis / Southaven campus.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Participate in initial equipment conceptual development and carefully balance product specifications, process requirements, layout complexity, cost, and lead-time limits
• Lay out new industrial electrical control panels which are NFPA79/NEC/UL508A compliant, and create electrical, pneumatic, and fluid schematics
• Simulate processes to inform design engineers of the conceptual viability of automation proposals for cooling plants, electrical distribution, and liquid-cooling loops
• Architect, write, and debug PLC code with an emphasis on generating code that is organized, structured, documented, maintainable, and reusable for critical infrastructure applications
• Generate aesthetically simple HMI screens for complex plant and facility systems while providing sufficient feedback for troubleshooting
• Manage electrical cabinet builds, field wiring, pneumatic, and fluid plumbing
• Select and size electrical and electromechanical components such as VFDs, servo motors, and controllers
• Deploy automated processes and equipment into live campus operations, including BMS, EPMS, SCADA, and PLC systems serving chillers, CDUs, pumps, and power distribution
• Set, implement, and maintain schedules and budgets to ensure project completion

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline
• 1+ years of professional experience in the design and commissioning of automation and controls systems for industrial applications

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Knowledge in building automation systems for critical infrastructure
• Mechanical (HVAC) controls and wiring, Delta controls
• Process integration and electromechanical/mechatronic systems experience
• Electrical schematic CAD experience using EPlan
• C#, .NET, Python, and/or SQL experience
• PLC programming experience, preferably Siemens TIA Portal and Beckhoff TwinCAT 3
• HMI and SCADA programming experience (Ignition preferred)
• Field bus networks, serial communication, and Ethernet communication
• Hands-on experience building and commissioning high-quality electrical control panels and electro-mechanical systems
• Knowledge of NEC, NFPA 79, UL508A codes
• Exposure to industrial sensors and equipment used in cooling plants and electrical distribution (temperature, flow, pressure, leak detection, VFDs, chillers, CDUs, switchgear)
• Experience in data centers, power generation, semiconductor, or other high-reliability industrial environments
• Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
• Experience in fast-paced iterative design and commissioning environments
• Experience solving complex problems with little to no supervision on schedule as an individual or as a member of an integrated team

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed
• Must be willing to travel to other locations
• Ability to work onsite in the Memphis, TN / Southaven, MS area

SpaceXAI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

ABOUT PERPLEXITY

Perplexity is AI for people who expect more. More accuracy. More agency. More signal, less noise. Our answer engine handles hundreds of millions of queries every month for people whose questions spark change and whose decisions bend the world toward progress. As our footprint grows, so does the number of policymakers, agencies, and civil society leaders who want to understand what we are building and how we think.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Public Policy Associate in Washington, D.C. to sit at the center of Perplexity's engagement with Congress, the executive branch, trade associations, think tanks, and the broader D.C. ecosystem. This work happens where Washington happens, in Hill offices, in coalition meetings across town, and at the occasional evening event where the conversations that matter most actually take place.

This is a relationship heavy, execution heavy seat. You've already worked both sides of the table, once inside a congressional office and once representing an organization before Congress, and you know how policy actually moves. Our Comms team and executive leadership set the strategy; you're our boots on the ground who makes it real. You'll build the stakeholder map, carry our message into the rooms that matter, and bring back what policymakers are saying, so that Perplexity shows up early, credibly, and consistently on the policy questions shaping AI. This role reports to the Senior Director, Product, Privacy & Regulatory Legal.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Execute our policy communications strategy set by our Comms and executive leadership teams. Turn company positions into talking points, event backgrounders, and rapid response, and feed intelligence back to our legal, policy, and product teams.

- Build and hold relationships with Hill staff in personal offices and on committees, executive branch staff, trade associations, think tanks, and civil society organizations.

- Advocate directly. Take meetings, deliver our positions, and follow bills and rulemakings that affect Perplexity, working within the company's lobbying disclosure and ethics requirements.

- Run our D.C. event footprint. Hill staff briefings, roundtables, product demos, receptions, dinners, and off sites. Own guest lists, venues, run of show, and follow up.

- Represent Perplexity in coalitions and trade association working groups. Track what's being said, flag what matters, and bring our point of view into the conversation.

- Partner with think tanks and civil society groups on convenings, research launches, and joint programming.

- Prepare our leaders for D.C. engagements. Briefing books, meeting prep, and post meeting recaps that actually get read.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- At least 3 years of professional experience, including time on Capitol Hill in a personal office or on a committee is strongly preferred.

- External lobbying experience, either at a government relations or law firm representing clients, or in house at a company. Registered lobbying experience under the Lobbying Disclosure Act is strongly preferred.

- A real Washington network you built yourself, and the instinct to keep growing it.

- Event execution. You can run a 20 person Hill staff briefing or a 150 person reception end to end without anything slipping.

- Strong writing. You can turn a meeting into a two paragraph readout and a briefing book into something a principal will actually use.

- Sound judgment. You know what to escalate, what to handle, and how to represent a company in a room without a script.

- Genuine curiosity about AI policy and the substance of what Perplexity is building. You don't need to be a technologist, but you do need to want to learn.

- Comfort with the pace. Mornings, days, and evenings. This is a role for someone energized by the D.C. schedule.

- Based in Washington, D.C. and in office four days a week, with occasional travel.

BONUS

- Hill experience on judiciary, commerce, intelligence, or AI focused portfolios.

- Experience staffing a principal at a company, agency, or trade association.

- Existing relationships across the AI and tech policy community in D.C.
